existing_kb_matches.label: def:degenerate_whittaker_setup
existing_kb_matches.statement: Given a nilpotent orbit O in g and f in O, choose a one-parameter subgroup phi: F^* -> G satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f for all s in F^*. Define U, respectively U', as the unipotent subgroup whose Lie algebra consists of those X such that lim_{s->0} phi(s).X = 0, respectively lim_{s->0} phi(s)s^-1.X = 0. Define U'' as the subgroup of U generated by U' and the stabilizer of f in U. The function gamma |-> psi(tr(f log gamma)) is a character of U'', denoted theta_f.

existing_kb_matches.label: def:degenerate_whittaker_forms
existing_kb_matches.statement: For a smooth representation (pi,W) and degenerate Whittaker setup (f,phi), W is said to admit a degenerate Whittaker model relative to (f,phi) if W_{U'',theta_f} is nonzero. The space W_{f,phi} of degenerate Whittaker forms on W relative to (f,phi) is defined by W_{U'',theta_f} when U = U'', and, when U != U'', by a Hom-space from the irreducible representation of the Heisenberg quotient U/(U'' intersection ker theta_f) with central character theta_f into W_{U'',theta_f}.

existing_kb_matches.label: def:whittaker_orbit_sets
existing_kb_matches.statement: Order nilpotent orbits by closure: O < O' means O is contained in the usual-topology closure of O'. For a representation pi with local character coefficients c_O, the paper introduces one set of nilpotent orbits O with c_O != 0 and a second set of nilpotent orbits containing an element f for which there exists a one-parameter subgroup phi satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f and W_{f,phi} != 0.

existing_kb_matches.label: ext:harish_chandra_local_character_expansion
existing_kb_matches.statement: For a smooth irreducible representation (pi,W) of G, there is a neighborhood of 1 in G identified by logarithm with a neighborhood of 0 in g on which the distribution character of pi has an expansion as a sum over nilpotent orbits O in g: tr pi = sum_O c_O times the Fourier transform of a suitably normalized invariant measure on O, with Fourier transform taken relative to psi composed with tr.

existing_kb_matches.label: ext:rodier_whittaker_model_criterion
existing_kb_matches.statement: Assume G is split. Let N be a maximal unipotent subgroup of G, T a torus normalizing N, and theta a nondegenerate character of N, meaning its stabilizer in T is the center of G. For the nilpotent orbit O containing the element f associated to theta by the source's pairing formula, a smooth irreducible representation (pi,W) admits a Whittaker model relative to theta if and only if c_O != 0. The source also reformulates this as existence of a maximal nilpotent orbit with nonzero coefficient.

existing_kb_matches.label: ext:moeglin_waldspurger_main_theorem
existing_kb_matches.statement: The main result of Chapter I says that the maximal elements of the nilpotent-orbit set defined by c_O != 0 coincide with the maximal elements of the nilpotent-orbit set defined by existence of nonzero W_{f,phi}. If O is a maximal element of either set, then c_O = dim W_{f,phi}, where f lies in O and phi is any one-parameter subgroup satisfying phi(s).f = s^-2 f.

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_i_3_compact_subgroup_bch
existing_kb_matches.statement: Assume e > 2d. Then there exists B > 3d such that for every n > B the exponential map is defined and injective on varpi^n E with inverse log, and exp(varpi^n E) is a subgroup of G. For n,m > B, the logarithm of exp X exp Z and the conjugation of Z by exp X satisfy the BCH and commutator error estimates recorded in 1.3(2)-(3).

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_i_6_character_stabilizer
existing_kb_matches.statement: For n >= B, the functional X |-> psi(tr(varpi^(-2n) Y X)) restricts to a Lie algebra character on the lattice used to define G_n, and gamma |-> psi(tr(varpi^(-2n) Y log gamma)) defines a character chi_n of G_n. If B <= m <= n and gamma in G_m stabilizes chi_n, then gamma lies in G_n exp(varpi^m (Y_sharp intersect L)).

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_i_10_nonzero_invariants
existing_kb_matches.statement: If the degenerate Whittaker space attached to the fixed nilpotent datum is nonzero, then for all sufficiently large n both auxiliary spaces W_n and W_n' are nonzero.

existing_kb_matches.label: prop:mw_i_11_orbit_from_whittaker
existing_kb_matches.statement: If the degenerate Whittaker space attached to Y is nonzero, then there exists a nilpotent orbit O in g that occurs with nonzero coefficient in the local character expansion of tr pi near the identity and whose closure contains Y.

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_i_12_dimension_coefficient
existing_kb_matches.statement: Let O = G.Y and suppose its coefficient c_O in 1.8 is nonzero and Y does not lie in the closure of any other orbit with nonzero coefficient in 1.8. Then for all sufficiently large n, dim W_n is finite, independent of n, and equal to c_O.

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_i_13_trivial_action
existing_kb_matches.statement: Fix c > B. If X belongs to the deep lattice inside L intersect Y_sharp specified in 1.13, then exp X normalizes G_n and stabilizes chi_n. Hence exp X acts on W_n, and for n sufficiently large this action is trivial.

existing_kb_matches.label: prop:mw_i_14_jacquet_injection
existing_kb_matches.statement: For n sufficiently large, in the diagram at the end of 1.9 the maps j and j' are injective, and the image of j' is the L'-fixed subspace of the Jacquet quotient appearing there.

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_i_15_transition_injective
existing_kb_matches.statement: For n sufficiently large, the transition map I_{n,n+1} is injective.

existing_kb_matches.label: prop:mw_ii_1_3_regular_principal_series_orbits
existing_kb_matches.statement: Let F_idx be an element of the indexing set J from II.1, with associated constituent pi_F and standard parabolic P_F. The maximal elements of N_tr(pi_F) are exactly the nilpotent orbits in g whose intersection with the Lie algebra u_F of the unipotent radical of P_F contains an open subset. These orbits are all contained in the Richardson orbit Omega_F of P_F.

existing_kb_matches.label: prop:mw_ii_2_gl_n_unique_nilpotent_orbit
existing_kb_matches.statement: For any smooth irreducible representation pi of GL_n(F), the maximal elements of N_tr(pi) are contained in a unique nilpotent orbit of gl_n, denoted X_tr(pi).

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_ii_3_2_concentration_criterion
existing_kb_matches.statement: Let beta be an orbit in S^2(X^*), and let (pi,W) be an irreducible representation of Sp(2n,F). Then W is concentrated on beta if and only if for every orbit O in the source's character-expansion set attached to pi and every Y in O, the S^2(X^*)-projection Y_minus lies in the closure of beta, and for at least one such Y it lies in beta itself.

existing_kb_matches.label: prop:mw_ii_3_1_small_rank_orbits
existing_kb_matches.statement: Let (pi,W) be a smooth irreducible representation of Sp(2n,F). Then (pi,W) is of rank k, for an integer k < n, if and only if every nilpotent orbit in the source's character-expansion set attached to pi has endomorphism rank at most k, and at least one such orbit has rank exactly k.

existing_kb_matches.label: lem:mw_ii_3_3_rank_projection
existing_kb_matches.statement: Let O be a G-orbit in g, and let k be the common rank of its elements viewed as endomorphisms of X plus X^*. Then there exists Y in O whose S^2(X^*) component has rank min(k,n).
